'''''Gennaria diphylla''''' is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] from the orchid family, [[Orchidaceae]], native to the region from the western [[Mediterranean]] and [[Macaronesia]] ([[Canary Islands]], [[Madeira]], [[Portugal]], [[Spain]], the [[Balearic Islands]], [[Morocco]], [[Algeria]], [[Tunisia]], [[Sardinia]], [[Tuscany]]).<ref name=WCSP_89154/><ref name=AFI_Gd/> ''Gennaria diphylla'' was illustrated (as ''Habenaria cordata'') in plate 3164 of Curtis' Botanical Magazine, 1832.

==Description==
''Gennaria diphylla'' has a stem about 15–30 cm tall. The stem bears two leaves. The lower leaf is larger, 4–7 cm long and 2.5–7 cm wide. The upper leaf is considerably smaller. Both leaves are elliptical or ovate in shape, with rounded lobes at the base making it heart-shaped. The flowers are borne in a spike up to 10 cm long. They are yellowish-green and form a bell-like shape. The lip (labellum) has three lobes, the middle one being slightly longer. A spur is present.<ref name=POWO_635582-1/><ref name=Bram01/>

==Taxonomy==
''Gennaria diphylla'' was first described, as ''Satyrium diphyllum'', by [[Johann Heinrich Friedrich Link|Johann Link]] in 1799. [[Filippo Parlatore]] transferred the species to his newly created genus ''Gennaria'' in 1860.<ref name="IPNI_635582-1">{{cite web |title=Plant Name Details for ''Gennaria diphylla'' |work=[[International Plant Names Index|The International Plant Names Index]] |url=http://www.ipni.org/ipni/idPlantNameSearch.do?id=635582-1 |accessdate=2018-03-14 }}</ref> The genus name honours [[Patrizio Gennari]].<ref name=DorrNich09/> The specific epithet ''diphylla'' means "two-leaved".<ref name=HyamPank95/>
